content.en: The Indian insurance sector underwent a paradigm shift following the **Malhotra Committee Report (1994)**, which recommended opening the sector to private players. This led to the establishment of the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** in 1999, which replaced the Controller of Insurance. Key reforms have focused on increasing **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** limits to attract capital and technology, enhancing solvency margins, and promoting **insurtech** to improve insurance penetration in rural areas.
